title: Rollout Velocity Gatekeeper Logbook
content:
Purpose:
This is the working gatekeeper logbook for the upcoming model rollout (hosted-api v2 route changes). Focus: keep release velocity high while bounding risk to SLOs and per-token cost. Use this doc during canary + slow-roll phases and hand off a distilled runbook to Ops on cutover.

Quick context and constraints:
- Release window: 2025-10-09 -> 2025-10-30 (phased traffic ramp).
- Target route: /v1/generate -> default model switches from rwd-base-1 to rwd-base-2-quant.
- Constraints: limited dedicated capacity in us-west1 for heavy context bursts; kv-cache warms slowly for long-history users.
- Assumption: Eng-serving-runtime will provide hotfix path if latency > 400ms p50 for 5m continuous.

Abstract flow (operator POV):
1) Canary (0.5% global traffic) — observe token-latency, error-rate, quality-sentiment for 90m.
2) Slow-roll (1% -> 10% -> 25%) — step every 60–120 minutes with stabilization windows and cost-gating.
3) Ramp -> 50% -> 100% only if burn-rate, error, and quality gates pass.

NOTE: this is intentionally checklist-heavy. Keep commentary short in the doc, capture deviations in the incident timeline section.

KPI snapshot (baseline vs canary window):
metric,baseline,canary-window,threshold,owner,notes
p50-token-latency-ms,120,145,<=200,eng-serving-runtime,slight uptick consistent with cache cold starts
p95-token-latency-ms,260,340,<=420,eng-serving-runtime,watch for tail regressions at 90m
request-error-rate-5m,0.18%,0.40%,<=0.75%,eng-sre,transient 429s at start of canary
quality-regression-score,0.00, -0.03, >=-0.05,applied-ml,small drop on summarization prompts
per-token-cost-usd,0.00095,0.00115,<=0.0016,finance,quantization improved unit cost but batch inefficiencies raised short transient
kv-cache-hit-rate,38%,24%,>=30%,eng-serving-runtime,expected warmup effect
traffic-steer-success-rate,99.98%,99.96%,>=99.9%,platform-engineering,no routing errors observed

Interpretation notes:
- Latency increased but under safety thresholds; p95 tail needs observation for next 2 ramp steps.
- Early 429 spikes correlated with autoscale delays; SRE to validate horizontal scaling throttle and warmup hooks.
- Quality dip concentrated on 3 prompt families (summarization, math, code-completion); applied-ml has quick-check tests running (see linked artifacts).

Gatekeeper decision checklist (operator actions + acceptance criteria):
1) Pre-canary checklist (must be green before starting):
   - [ ] Canary k8s deployment image pinned (infra PR merged) (owner: platform-engineering)
   - [ ] Canary traffic table and percentage set in rollout controller (owner: product-ops)
   - [ ] Alerting targets for p50/p95/error-rate/cost burn created and tested (owner: eng-sre)
   - [ ] QA smoke-run with 500 synthetic sessions hitting heavy-history flows (owner: applied-ml)
   - [ ] Comm plan posted to #launch-ops-thread + exec-notify list (owner: product-ops)

2) Canary run (0.5% for 90m) — monitoring window actions:
   - [ ] Collect 5m rolling metrics snapshot at 0/15/30/60/90m (owner: product-ops)
   - [ ] Run the 12 prompt sanity checks from applied-ml (pass >= 11/12) (owner: applied-ml)
   - [ ] If request-error-rate > 0.75% or p95 > 420ms for 10m => PAUSE and escalate to eng-sre and eng-serving-runtime
   - [ ] If quality-regression-score <= -0.05 => PAUSE and run rollback-play (owner: applied-ml + product-ops)

3) Slow-roll steps (1%, 10%, 25%) — for each step maintain the same policy with shorter windows (60m):
   - Throttles: do not increase if per-token-cost increases > 30% vs baseline OR kv-cache hit < 28% OR error-rate trending up 2x baseline over 30m
   - Required green checks: health endpoints stable, no new 5xx spike, canary sanity prompts pass, support runbook ready

4) Full-ramp gates (50% -> 100%):
   - Only after two consecutive slow-roll steps show p95 within threshold and quality-regression-score > -0.03
   - Finance gives go if projected monthly unit-cost delta < 12%
   - Exec OK (ops leader + product leader) posted in rollout log and #launch-ops-thread

Emergency rollback play (fast path):
- Trigger conditions: sustained request-error-rate >= 1.5% for 5m, p95 > 600ms for 10m, critical quality-severity (safety or hallucination spikes), or SRE judgement.
- Actions:
  1) Product-ops flips route-weight to last-stable at controller (target 100% shift within 60s).
  2) Platform-engineering confirms rollback completed and verifies routing success-rate > 99.9%.
  3) Eng-sre opens incident timeline and notifies Execs + CS for customer impact triage.
  4) Applied-ml attaches latest failing examples to incident and creates reproduction PR.

Runbook knobs and observability links:
- Observability dashboards: token-latency, kv-cache, model-quality-summaries (link: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/launch/rollout-velocity)
- Synthetic runner: https://infra-tools.redwood.ai/synthetics/rollout-velocity-runner
- Canary controller: https://api.redwood.ai/rollouts/active/--- (internal)

Risks and mitigation slate (short bullets):
- Risk: bursty long-context sessions starve dedup/batching window -> mitigation: pre-warm KV caches for top-100 customers and limit concurrent long-session slots during roll.
- Risk: quantized variant introduces subtle decoding edge-cases on code prompts -> mitigation: applied-ml quick-fix list + targeted A/B on code routes.
- Risk: cost overshoot from suboptimal batching -> mitigation: reduce max-requests-per-batch and re-evaluate after 2 hours at 10% traffic.

Communications and customer-facing notes:
- Customer Success will prepare a brief FAQ for early adopters and slow-roll cohort. (owner: customer-success)
- If rollback occurs, CS to proactively message customers in affected cohort within 1 hour with status and ETA.

Post-launch evaluation (within 72h of 100%):
- Retrospective items to capture: delta in unit cost, p95 stability, top 10 failing prompts, incidents opened, customer tickets, learnings for batching/kernel selection.
- Deliverable: 1-page TLDR for execs + data appendix (product-ops).

Open questions / TODO (notes to self):
- TODO: confirm autoscale warmup policy is 2 pods/min in us-west1 (ask infra team)
- TODO: add latency-lag correlation plot to dashboard (owner: observability)
- Question: Should we split code-heavy traffic to a separate route to minimize risk? quick strawpoll with eng-serving-runtime.

Operational timeline (compact):
- 2025-10-08 18:00 — final go/no-go dry run
- 2025-10-09 02:00 — start canary (0.5%)
- 2025-10-09 04:00 — evaluate canary -> decision recorded
- 2025-10-09 06:00 -> staged slow-roll begin if green (1% -> 10% -> 25%)
- 2025-10-09 18:00 -> target 50% if gates pass
- 2025-10-10 03:00 -> target 100% if green

Appendix: quick links and artifacts referenced:
- PRODOPS-547 (rollout plan)
- SRE-1889 (autoscale warmup investigation)
- GH PR infra/pull/4123 (canary deployment images)
- Synthetic test suite id: synthetics/rv-sanity-v3

Notes to reviewers: leave inline comments in this Drive doc (or drop short notes in #launch-ops-thread). This doc will be distilled into the runbook that goes to the oncall playbook library.
kpi_snapshot: p50_latency_ms: 120 -> 145 (threshold 200); p95_latency_ms: 260 -> 340 (threshold 420); error_rate_5m: 0.18% -> 0.40% (threshold 0.75%); quality_delta: 0.00 -> -0.03 (threshold -0.05); cost_per_token_usd: 0.00095 -> 0.00115 (threshold 0.0016); kv_cache_hit: 38% -> 24% (threshold 30%); traffic_steer_success: 99.98% -> 99.96% (threshold 99.9%)
rollout_checklist: Pre-canary: pin images; set controller traffic; test alerts; QA smoke-run; post comms. Canary: collect snapshots every 15m; run sanity prompts; PAUSE if errors or quality fails. Slow-roll: step schedule + throttle gates; do not increase if cost + cache or error thresholds breach. Full-ramp: require two consecutive green steps, finance + exec signoff. Emergency rollback: rollback route-weight, confirm routing, open incident, attach failing examples.
decision_gates: Gate A (post-canary): pass health checks, error <= 0.75%, quality >= -0.05 -> move to slow-roll. Gate B (post-slow-roll): p95 <= 420ms and quality >= -0.03 and finance delta < 12% -> move to 50%. Gate C (pre-100%): two green slow-roll steps and exec ok. Any critical trigger or sustained degradation -> immediate rollback.
incident_timeline_template:
timestamp | owner | action | result
2025-10-09T02:15Z | eng-sre | observed 429 spike | rate fell after 3m, related to autoscale lag
2025-10-09T03:05Z | product-ops | paused rollout at 1% | rolled back to 0.5% until fixes
notes: Informal working doc: expect edits, shorthand, and TODOs. Intended audience: product-ops, eng-sre, eng-serving-runtime, applied-ml, platform-engineering, customer-success.
